title: lint: a hop leaf through an injected lookup (record.owner_id.<field>) is judged at neither door
body:
domain:spec#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQjrEpxMVxEiDUJHqC

Out-of-scope item carried by seat ruling 6901005939 on card #33435 (PR #34129).

PR #34129 judges the null guard on the six injected system columns themselves (`owner_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `owning_business_unit_id`, `queue`, `organization_id`) in flow and hook conditions. A condition that hops *through* one of them, such as `record.owner_id.name > ...` or a misspelt `record.owner_id.nmae`, is judged at neither `os build` nor the publish door. The hop's target object is not resolved for an injected lookup, so neither the leaf's existence nor its nullability is checked.

**Ask.** Resolve the target of an injected lookup (the platform's user / business-unit / queue / organization objects) in the expression walk. Then judge the leaf as a declared lookup's leaf is judged: an unknown field is refused, and a nullable leaf needs the guard. Pin it with one refused misspelling, one guarded read accepted, and one unguarded ordering refused. Measure first whether any example or first-party package already writes such a hop.
